items_missed: No agenda statement with a rough time frame and no 'sound good?' confirmation up front
Confirmed the origin address (600 Industry Way Suite 40, Prosper) but never confirmed the destination address out loud, despite building a two-crew, two-location plan around it
Never asked about stairs, floors, elevator, loading dock, parking, or walk distance — the origin is a suite in an office building and this drives the clock more than anything else discussed
Never asked about packing needs or boxes, even though the load is camera equipment, computers, apparel, and loose product that will need containment
No No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) — the single biggest miss on this call given it is a production crew's camera and tech gear
No Meet Your Mover email description
No Ecobox referral despite an obvious apparel-and-product boxing need

Save Your Ass prep speech never given — telling Bailey's team to pre-box the small apparel and product before Thursday would have directly cut billable hours on a job she said had 'a lot of' loose items
Did not mention the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email (described the email contents generally instead)
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Never gave business hours or how to reach the branch
Used her name twice ('Hey, Bailey' and the sign-off) — needs 3+
No time-range reference point offered; explicitly said offices don't have one rather than anchoring her with a comparable job
top_strength: Turned a genuinely awkward two-for-one request (move four offices out, then shuffle people internally) into a clean two-crew plan and sold the efficiency logic behind it — 'what you guys do in four hours, four guys can do in two,' plus saving the second crew's commute. His no-hidden-fees pitch was the sharpest of the three calls: he specifically named the loop-back trip, heavy items, tech items, and stairs as things that carry no surcharge, which is exactly the reassurance a commercial buyer needs.
coaching_note: Perfect clock section and a strong pricing block, but he moved a production company's camera gear and computers without ever mentioning No Worries Damage Coverage — on a commercial tech move that is the differentiator that matters most. Anchor every quote with the coverage conversation before you ask for the booking.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and genuinely consultative — when Bailey apologized that her request was 'probably very weird' he immediately normalized it ('we get some unique ones from time to time, this isn't anything crazy'), and he collaborated on her crew-splitting idea instead of steering her back to script.
